golden.producer: drat-trim -L from a CaDiCaL 3.0.1 DRAT proof; see protocol/toolchains.json

variants.change: cut at half the byte length
negate the first lemma literal of the first addition
drop the first hint of the first addition
pair with the other obligation's CNF
pad past 4 MiB with deletion lines
make the first addition's last hint a clause that was never added
append a RAT (negative) hint to the first addition

obligations.name: the same identity without the carry shift

rules: Variable 1 is constant false and clause 1 is its negative unit. Bit i (least significant first) of x is variable 2 + i and of y is variable 34 + i.

Gates are numbered from 66 in creation order and emit their Tseitin clauses as they are created: AND g=a.b gives (-g a) (-g b) (g -a -b); XOR gives (-g a b) (-g -a -b) (g -a b) (g a -b); OR gives (g -a) (g -b) (-g a b).

The left side is blasted before the right side, and each operation's left operand before its right. xor and and make one gate per bit; shl by k makes no gates and shifts in literal 1; add is a ripple-carry adder whose carry starts as literal 1 and makes, per bit, t=XOR(a,b), s=XOR(t,c), u=AND(a,b), v=AND(c,t), c=OR(u,v) in that order.
The miter makes d_i=XOR(lhs_i, rhs_i) for every bit, then o=d_0 and o=OR(o, d_i) for i from 1, and ends with the unit clause (o).
The CNF text is p cnf V C then one line per clause, literals in decimal separated by single spaces, each line ending in space, 0 and a line feed.

An LRAT certificate is ASCII lines ending in line feeds. An addition is ID LITERALS 0 HINTS 0 with IDs strictly increasing and above the clause count; a deletion is ID d IDS 0 and its leading ID is otherwise ignored. Numbers are canonical decimal.

Each addition is checked by reverse unit propagation from the negation of its literals: every hint but the last must be unit and assigns its open literal, the last must be falsified, and a satisfied hint fails. Negative hints are refused as rat_unsupported.

The certificate is accepted when an addition derives the empty clause on its final line. Rejections carry the first failing line number, or 0 for cnf_mismatch, oversized and no_empty_clause; certificates above 4 MiB are refused before parsing.

run_time_cases.name: fresh certificate
run_time_cases.rule: The pinned solver runs on the candidate-emitted CNF; the fresh certificate must be accepted in the prover and by the standalone checker, and every V-01 to V-11 mutation of it rejected exactly as the reference rejects it.

run_time_cases.name: satisfiable input
run_time_cases.rule: The solver runs on B-C02's CNF and reports satisfiable; the claim stays non-successful as disproved_obligation, and the reported x and y are checked in the prover to falsify the identity.

run_time_cases.name: unknown
run_time_cases.rule: The solver runs with a conflict limit of 0 and reports unknown; the claim stays non-successful as unknown.

run_time_cases.name: timeout
run_time_cases.rule: The solver runs under a wall ceiling of 0 seconds; the claim stays non-successful as timeout.

run_time_cases.name: missing output
run_time_cases.rule: The certificate file is absent after a solver run; the claim stays non-successful as failed_certificate.

solver.trust: untrusted: its search, heuristics and output are outside every logical trusted base.

theorems.name: the obligation holds, through a checked certificate
an accepted certificate proves its obligation
